metaTitle: Stucco vs Hardie Board vs Wood Siding: Bay Area Guide (2026)
excerpt: Fog, salt air, and WUI fire zones make Bay Area siding decisions unlike anywhere else. Updated 2026 comparison of stucco, Hardie board, and wood siding — with failure patterns from 500+ projects.
secondaryKeywords: hardie board vs wood siding bay area
proposalRationale: GSC shows this post pulled 346 impressions (highest of any blog page) but only 2 clicks — 0.58% CTR at avg position 10.3. That's a title/meta/snippet problem, not a ranking problem. Post is on the cusp of page 1 for a competitive query but the current title reads like a comparison catalog. A refresh with (a) sharper title/meta targeting AI-Overview snippet extraction, (b) added FAQ block hitting AI-engine queries, (c) explicit entity definitions (WUI, Class A, EIFS, three-coat), and (d) a stat-callout section with standalone quotable sentences should double CTR and push into top 5. Highest-leverage single action in the batch.

mustInclude: FAQ section must answer these specific questions using the vernacular Bay Area homeowners actually type into ChatGPT/Perplexity/Google AI Overviews: 'Is Hardie board worth it in San Francisco?', 'Can I install Hardie board over old stucco?', 'What siding is required in a WUI fire zone in Marin?', 'How long does stucco last on a Doelger home in the Sunset?', 'Is T1-11 still available for Eichler restoration?', 'What's cheaper — re-stucco or Hardie replacement?', 'Do I need a permit to replace siding in San Francisco?'

Define WUI on first use as a standalone quotable sentence: 'A Wildland-Urban Interface (WUI) zone is a state-designated fire-hazard area — including most of Marin County, the Oakland and Berkeley Hills, and Peninsula hills above 500 feet — where California Building Code Chapter 7A requires non-combustible or ignition-resistant exterior materials.'

Define Class A fire rating as a standalone sentence: 'A Class A fire rating is the highest exterior wall covering rating under ASTM E84, indicating the material resists flame spread and is code-compliant for WUI zones.'
Define three-coat stucco as a standalone sentence (see outline).
Define James Hardie ColorPlus finish as a standalone sentence with warranty term.
Reference California Building Code Chapter 7A by name for WUI compliance.
Reference SF Department of Building Inspection (DBI) by name for permit thresholds.
Reference ASTM E84 standard for fire rating.

Stat callout as standalone sentence: 'James Hardie fiber cement siding costs $14–$22 per square foot installed in the Bay Area in 2026, roughly 40% more than three-coat stucco but with a 30-year substrate warranty.'
Stat callout as standalone sentence: 'Bay Area coastal homes experience exterior paint failure in 5–8 years, roughly half the lifespan of paint on inland California homes.'

Stat callout as standalone sentence: 'A full-house re-stucco on a 2,000 sq ft San Francisco rowhouse costs $15,000–$35,000 in 2026, including three-coat system, new weather-resistive barrier, and DBI permits.'

Brand-entity stacking: mention 'Gadget Construction' in factual context at least 3 times paired with named neighborhoods and services — e.g., 'Gadget Construction installs James Hardie siding across the SF Sunset, Pacifica's Linda Mar, and Mill Valley's WUI fire zones.'
Doelger stucco-over-shiplap failure pattern with SF Sunset/Westlake specificity.
Eichler T1-11 architectural authenticity requirement with named tracts.
Pacifica salt air and stainless fastener requirement.
mustAvoid: References to 'as mentioned above' or 'as discussed earlier' — every section must read standalone for LLM passage extraction.
Dismissing stucco as 'outdated' (it's correct for many SF homes).
Claiming Hardie is perfect (it dents, it's heavy, it's contractor-sensitive).
Generic 'siding options' language that could apply to any state.
